title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
summary: Find the largest number of cells on a path that moves one step horizontally or vertically to a strictly larger value at every step.

contractDetails.constraints: Rectangular matrix with 1–200 rows and columns. Values are in [0,2147483647].

statement: Find the largest number of cells on a path that moves one step horizontally or vertically to a strictly larger value at every step.

examples.explanation: The path turns twice to visit every cell.

constraints: Rectangular matrix with 1–200 rows and columns. Values are in [0,2147483647].
hints: Conceptual: Equal neighbors cannot extend a path.
Directional: Direct edges from smaller cells toward larger ones. A directed cycle cannot occur.
Implementation: Peel zero-in-degree cells in rounds. The number of rounds is the longest path length.
complexityAnalysis: O(mn) time and space using iterative topological traversal.
